title: Could it be? He knelt there sinless and timid; and he would hold upon his tongue the host and God would enter his purified body
html_source: In order to demonstrate the development of Stephen’s consciousness Joyce ends each chapter with an epiphany. Stephen recognizes the delusion of one way of life and recognizes the truth of another. In this moment Stephen understands that he must turn to a religious life. Unlike other novels where the narrators look back at the events of their childhood with an adult outlook, Portrait takes up a different style. When Stephen declares, “Another life!” and “The past was past,” we are given no hints that Stephen’s religious life will eventually be replaced by his artistic life. Rather, much like Stephen, we are led to believe that he will remain religious for the rest of his life. In this sense, we experience the successive epiphanies in Stephen’s life just as he experiences them.
